hook: The commitment card matters only after Beatrice says the proof time out loud.
counterintuition: A commitment is not stronger because it sounds dramatic. It gets stronger when the action, deadline, verifier, and consequence are clear enough that retreat is harder to disguise as rescheduling.

examples.title: Beatrice says the proof time

planSpec.audience: a practitioner in executive assistant commitment board who needs the chapter move under real pressure
planSpec.stakes: the visible result will slip while everyone can still explain the effort
planSpec.requiredBeat: Beatrice states the commitment and the verification time out loud.

examples.scenario: Commitment cards slide across Beatrice's desk as the executive team stands to leave. She must decide whether the cards are reminders or promises. She reads one aloud: vendor shortlist sent by Thursday at 3 p.m., verified by the chief of staff before the travel meeting.
examples.whatToDo: State the commitment, proof, and verification time out loud before the meeting breaks.
examples.whyItMatters: A commitment has power because it makes retreat harder to disguise as rescheduling. Beatrice gives the promise a witness and a clock.

examples.title: Eleanor sends the renewal promise

planSpec.audience: a decision-maker in software sales renewal push choosing whether to protect execution or drift
planSpec.stakes: the next 12 weeks will inherit a soft plan unless the decision is made now
planSpec.requiredBeat: Eleanor sends the renewal promise to the manager and client.

examples.scenario: "Who else knows you are doing it?" the manager asks while renewal dates are sorted by account size. Eleanor must decide whether the renewal push remains private ambition or becomes a promise sent to her manager and the client contact with the exact date of the next proposal.
examples.whatToDo: Send the renewal promise to the people who can verify it, with the action and due date in plain language.
examples.whyItMatters: Commitments to others create useful pressure. Eleanor makes the renewal work visible before delay can feel harmless.

examples.title: Vera names the weekly promise

planSpec.audience: a team lead in community college apprenticeship office who needs visible proof before the week softens
planSpec.stakes: the team will mistake motion for progress if the proof stays hidden
planSpec.requiredBeat: Vera turns the apprenticeship goal into a named weekly promise.

examples.scenario: You are looking at apprentice files in a cabinet that has swallowed three recruiting pushes already. Vera must decide whether the goal stays as “more placements” or becomes a named weekly promise: ten employer calls by Wednesday, two student matches by Friday, verified in the office huddle.
examples.whatToDo: Turn the apprenticeship goal into a weekly promise with numbers, dates, and a verifier.
examples.whyItMatters: Vera makes commitment operational. The file cabinet stops being a storage place for good intentions.

examples.title: Noelle tells the sous-chef first

planSpec.audience: a reflective operator in restaurant prep kitchen promise reading last week's failure as evidence
planSpec.stakes: a repeat failure will be explained away instead of corrected
planSpec.requiredBeat: Noelle commits the prep standard to the sous-chef before service.

examples.scenario: It took one dinner rush with missing prep labels for Noelle to see that her private standard had no weight. Stainless pans were ready, service was coming, and nobody knew what she had promised. The next afternoon she tells the sous-chef the prep standard before service and asks him to check the labels at 4:30.
examples.whatToDo: Tell the sous-chef the prep standard, deadline, and verification point before service starts.
examples.whyItMatters: Noelle turns a private preference into a visible standard. The promise gains force because someone else can see whether it happened.

examples.title: Ronan gives the coordinator proof

planSpec.audience: a reader in regional hospice volunteer plan comparing intention before the move with proof after it
planSpec.stakes: the work will stay aspirational unless the action changes in the room
planSpec.requiredBeat: Ronan tells the coordinator the volunteer calls and proof due Friday.

examples.scenario: Volunteer badges sit in a shoebox beside the regional hospice schedule. Before, Ronan hoped to call former volunteers when the week calmed down. After, he tells the coordinator: twelve calls by Friday noon, call notes in the shared sheet, and a quick check before the weekend roster is built.
examples.whatToDo: Tell the coordinator the volunteer calls, the proof, and the Friday verification point.
examples.whyItMatters: Ronan makes the promise harder to soften. The coordinator does not add guilt; she adds visibility.

examples.title: Gavin posts the studio promise

planSpec.audience: two colleagues in Milan architecture studio forcing the commitment into plain speech
planSpec.stakes: a public promise will dissolve unless someone names the proof and owner
planSpec.requiredBeat: Gavin writes the studio commitment where the partner can verify it.

examples.scenario: What would the partner be able to verify without asking twice? Gavin says in the Milan architecture studio, model photos pinned above the drafting desk. The team must decide whether design progress stays conversational or becomes a posted commitment: facade options printed by Thursday, owner named, review slot booked.
examples.whatToDo: Write the studio commitment where the partner can verify action, owner, and deadline.
examples.whyItMatters: Gavin turns collaboration into a standard. The commitment is not a slogan once the proof is visible on the wall.
